payload.title: lucia codex --strict accepts an option it never uses

payload.change: cmd_run reads and judges the command before it touches the daemon, then refuses --strict for any provider but claude: `run: --strict is only supported by claude, not codex; it passes claude's --strict-mcp-config, which has no equivalent here`, exit 2. No daemon autostart, no roster entry, no credential on that path. Covers both spellings (`lucia codex --strict` and `lucia run --strict --provider codex -- ...`). claude --strict is unchanged.
not_done: not merged into main, not pushed
your review item __main__.py:1294 (global FRONT_NAME persists across main() calls in one process) is untouched
payload.side_effect_worth_knowing: Moving the argument checks above read_endpoint also means the pre-existing usage errors (`name the provider command after --`, `cannot tell which provider ... is`) no longer autostart a daemon. Error precedence changed for those cases: a bad command line is now reported before `no running daemon`.

payload.option_audit: No. Of the options declared by _add_run_flags, only --strict is provider-specific. ttl, autostart, nudge, max_nudges, and state_dir are consumed by provider-neutral cmd_run/_run_on_a_pty behavior. (Provider-specific argv construction exists, but is not another _add_run_flags option.)

No correctness issue found in the patch.

payload.why: That is by design. test_strict_still_reaches_the_provider_that_has_it is the guard on the other side of the fix, not a regression test for it: the claude branch at :999 already appended --strict-mcp-config on the parent, so it is green before and after. A third failure on the parent means the environment took it down, not the code -- consistent with your own note that the sandbox failures were environmental (ps and local sockets prohibited).

acceptance: check runs after provider resolution and before store/bind_terminal, so no credential or binding is created on the error path
covers both spellings: `lucia codex --strict` and `lucia run --strict --provider codex -- <cmd>`
regression test red before the fix, green after
payload.decision_detail: `--strict` with a codex provider must fail loudly: print `run: --strict is only supported by claude` to stderr and return exit code 2, before any credential is minted or binding created. No silent acceptance, no warn-and-continue.
payload.source: adversarial review of ff35542, follow-up item 2
payload.symptom: `_add_run_flags` at __main__.py:1267 registers `--strict` for both providers, but only the claude branch at :999 reads `args.strict` (it appends `--strict-mcp-config`). The codex branch at :1002 never reads it, so `lucia codex --strict` accepts the option and silently does nothing: the session keeps its other MCP servers while the user believes it is isolated.
